# NAGI 凪
## Japan Market-Entry Campaign — Sleep-Quality & Temporary-Stress Supplement
### Ethical Design Document, Creative Platform & Activation Plan
**Prepared for Brand Council | Version 2.0 (supersedes v1.0 "Just a Little Calmer Tonight")**

---

> ⚠️ **Compliance and status caveat.** Japanese food-labelling and advertising law is in active reform following the 2024 red-yeast-rice (紅麹) incident. Every legal reference in this document is a **planning input, not a legal opinion**. No claim string, label, pack, script or landing page may be published until (a) Japanese regulatory counsel has signed the specific asset in writing and (b) the wording matches the accepted notification record. Figures marked *[ILL]* are illustrative planning numbers to be replaced with primary research and counsel confirmation in Gate 0. Assumptions and confidence levels are registered in §14.
>
> **Planning FX rate: ¥155 = US$1.00**, fixed for this document; re-fixed at each gate.

---

## 1. The Idea, in One Page

### 1.1 The consumer truth we are building on

Japanese adults do not experience poor sleep as an *illness*. They experience it as a slow erosion — a run of mornings that start badly, a 15:00 fog, a shortening fuse with a spouse or a subordinate. They do not want to be rescued. They want the run to break.

Crucially, the culturally available frame for this already exists and is centuries old: **未病 (mibyō)** — "not yet ill, not quite well" — and **養生 (yōjō)** — the daily cultivation of health. These are not exotic decorations. They are the ordinary, respectable, non-medical vocabulary in which a 48-year-old section manager can admit he sleeps badly without admitting he is unwell, and can do something about it without going to a clinic.

### 1.2 The brand idea

> **凪 (nagi)** is the still interval when the land breeze and the sea breeze change places — the pause between two winds. It is not a permanent calm. It is the gap that lets the next thing begin.

That is an honest metaphor for what this product does: a small, repeated, cumulative intervention. It is also, precisely, what the science supports and what the law permits us to say.

### 1.3 Campaign platform

**「いい朝が、すこしずつ増える。」**
*"Little by little, more good mornings."*

**Why this line and not v1.0's "Just a Little Calmer Tonight."** The previous line was rejected in redraft for a specific reason: *tonight* promises an acute, same-night effect. Our positioning is maintenance, not rescue; our notified claim is a continuity claim requiring daily intake; and an acute-relief promise edges toward drug-efficacy territory under 薬機法. The line contradicted the strategy and the dossier. The replacement line is **cumulative** ("little by little"), **counted in mornings not nights** (an outcome the user can actually verify), and **quantitatively modest** ("more," not "good mornings, guaranteed").

**Endline / signature:** 「夜は、すこし静かに。」 — used only as an atmospheric sign-off, never as a claim.

### 1.4 The proof architecture (why anyone should believe us)

| Layer | What it is | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **Notified function** | The exact CAA-notified claim string, verbatim | Pack front, all claim-bearing assets |
| **The honest number** | Plain-Japanese statement of the *size* of the effect and the proportion of people who saw it | Pack QR → "この製品でわかっていること" page |
| **The dossier** | Full systematic review / trial record, Japanese, downloadable, plus the studies that did *not* support us | Same page, no email gate |
| **The refund** | 「合わない方へ」 — 60-day full refund, no return, no reason required (D2C) | Pack, site, all D2C creative |
| **The referral out** | Sleep self-check that routes likely clinical cases to medical care, *before* the buy button | Site, LINE, pharmacy leaflet |

No competitor in this category currently publishes its negative studies or routes traffic away from purchase. That, not adjective inflation, is our distinctiveness.

---

## 2. Market, Consumer and Competitive Reality

### 2.1 Why Japan is a distinctive advertising market

| Dimension | Japan-specific reality | Campaign implication |
|---|---|---|
| **Category maturity** | Large, habituated supplement market; supplements read as *maintenance* (養生), not *rescue* | Sell routine and continuity |
| **Health philosophy** | 未病 / 養生 inherited from Kampō; wellness is a daily practice, not an intervention | Position in the mibyō space — legitimate and non-medical |
| **Trust position** | Post-紅麹 scrutiny of the self-notified FFC regime; tightened adverse-event reporting and GMP requirements | Radical transparency is the differentiator, not a cost |
| **Advertising register** | Superlatives and hard-sell read as vulgar and untrustworthy; *情緒 (jōcho)* — atmospheric, indirect, feeling-led advertising — is the prestige register | Craft-led, quiet, low-volume creative |
| **Retail structure** | Drugstore chains (マツキヨココカラ, ウエルシア, ツルハ, サンドラッグ, コスモス) are the gatekeepers; shelf and 什器 presence drive trial more than awareness | Trade investment is not "below the line," it *is* the line |
| **Word-of-mouth power** | Category breakouts are 口コミ-driven, amplified by X and 店頭 | Highest legal/ethical exposure sits here (§8.4) |

### 2.2 Audience: four named segments, not "adults 28–55"

| # | Segment | Size *[ILL]* | Sleep problem | Receptivity | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | **「中間管理職の睡眠負債」** — 42–55, male-skewed (~65/35), mid-management, commuter, ¥7–12M HH income | 6.2M | Early waking, 3am rumination, no wind-down; will not consult a doctor about sleep | High to non-medical, dignity-preserving framing; hostile to anything that looks like weakness | **P1** |
| **B** | **「途切れる眠りの母」** — 33–44, female, dual-income, child under 8 | 4.1M | Fragmented sleep, low agency over schedule; guilt about self-spend | High to *permission* framing ("this is maintenance, not indulgence"); very high 口コミ propensity | **P1** |
| **C** | **「夜更かしの自律」** — 26–34, female-skewed, single/DINK, high screen-time | 5.5M | Self-imposed late nights, "revenge bedtime"; sleep as self-optimisation | High to design/ritual framing; lowest willingness to pay; entry cohort | P2 |
| **D** | **交代勤務者** — nurses, care workers, logistics, retail | 3.8M | Circadian disruption, genuinely severe | Commercially attractive, **ethically constrained** | **P3 — deliberately not targeted** |

**Why we will not target Segment D.** Their sleep disruption is structural and often clinically significant; a continuity claim built on nocturnal sleep quality is a poor fit for rotating shifts; and marketing a mild supplement into a population with elevated genuine sleep-disorder prevalence risks displacing care. They may buy the product — we will not exclude them from shelves — but we will run **no targeted media, no shift-worker creative, and no occupational-health B2B push into shift-heavy employers in Years 1–2.** This costs us revenue. It is recorded in §10 and audited in §11.

**Primary target for Year 1: Segments A and B.** Creative lead: A. Advocacy engine: B.

### 2.3 Competitive set — the real problem we face

| Competitor | Proposition | Why it matters to us |
|---|---|---|
| **Yakult 1000 / Y1000** | Lactic-acid-bacterium drink; notified stress-relief and sleep-quality claims; category-defining 口コミ breakout | Redefined "sleep quality" as a mainstream, non-medical, *drinkable ritual*. It owns the ritual, has a delivery-lady route to home, and dominates conversational share. We are a capsule competing with a habit. |
| **味の素 グリナ** | Glycine, sleep quality; long-running, D2C-strong, medically credible tone | Owns the "serious sleep supplement" credibility position among 50+. |
| **アサヒ ネナイト** | L-theanine tablet, mass drugstore distribution, low price | Direct format and ingredient overlap; our price premium must be earned, not asserted. |
| **ハウス ネルノダ** | GABA drink, konbini-led, impulse | Owns immediacy and convenience — precisely the acute position we are declining. |
| **FANCL / DHC / 小林製薬 ナイトミン** | Trusted domestic houses, decades of equity, deep drugstore relationships | Trust equity we cannot buy. We can only buy *verifiability*. |
| **Suntory Wellness** | Premium D2C machine, CRM excellence | Sets the benchmark on subscription economics and 顧客対応. |

**The competitive conclusion.** We cannot out-spend, out-trust or out-distribute the domestic incumbents in Year 1. There is exactly one position they have structurally declined to occupy: **published, checkable, effect-size-honest ev
